name: exported-api-docs
description: Checks concise, accurate Go API documentation
prompt: Document an exported Go function that accepts a context, returns a value and an error, and has several edge cases.
trap: A doc comment should explain contract and failure behavior without inventing mandatory sections or duplicating the implementation.

assertions.text: Starts the comment with the exported identifier
States purpose, important inputs, outputs, errors, cancellation, and side effects
Avoids promising behavior not established by code or tests
Uses an executable Example test when a runnable usage path adds value

name: readme-from-real-commands
description: Checks task-oriented README content and command verification
prompt: Write a README for a Go CLI with installation, configuration, a minimal example, testing, and troubleshooting guidance.
trap: A README is not useful if it copies a generic template or contains commands that do not work from a clean checkout.

assertions.text: Identifies audience, supported Go/platform versions, and the actual command or import path
Includes a copyable minimal path with defaults, errors, and configuration precedence
Documents operational concerns appropriate to the application without inventing unsupported features
Verifies commands and avoids real credentials or private endpoints in snippets

name: private-disclosure-boundary
description: Checks privacy and authorization before external documentation publication
prompt: Can I publish an internal package's source and Playground example to make its documentation easier to find?
trap: Public registries and Playground links disclose source and dependencies; tested examples are useful without automatically publishing private code.

assertions.text: Requires explicit authorization and a license/privacy/disclosure review before publication
Explains that internal packages and customer/private data should remain in approved documentation channels
Offers local executable Example tests as the portable default
Treats Playground or public documentation registration as optional and review-gated

name: release-artifact-links
description: Checks release documentation against generated artifacts
prompt: Add an installation link for the v1.2.3 CLI release produced by GoReleaser.
trap: Archive names and paths come from the actual GoReleaser configuration; a guessed URL can 404 or point to the wrong platform.

assertions.text: Inspects the release configuration's archive naming, target, and asset location
Uses the exact tag/version and generated filename rather than an invented path
Documents checksums and platform selection when the release produces them
Verifies the link or states what release evidence is still needed

name: changelog-security-category
prompt: A release fixes a null handling bug, a retry bug, and a vulnerability in deserialization. How should the changelog group them?
trap: Security fixes deserve clear visibility and should not be buried among ordinary fixes, while the format remains the project's chosen convention.

assertions.text: Separates the vulnerability under a security heading when the changelog format supports it
Keeps ordinary correctness fixes under the normal fixed/changed categories
Avoids exposing exploit details or sensitive incident data beyond the disclosure policy

name: examples-as-tests
prompt: Should every exported package include a Playground demo and an Example function?
trap: Examples are valuable when they demonstrate a supported contract, but neither a Playground nor an example is mandatory for every package.

assertions.text: Recommends Example functions for stable, runnable usage where they improve documentation
Uses Output comments only for deterministic output
Keeps network, credentials, time, and private endpoints out of examples
Treats Playground links as optional and disclosure-gated

name: generated-api-docs
description: Checks source-of-truth selection for generated documentation
prompt: Our project exposes protobuf and HTTP APIs. Should I hand-write a second API reference and generate OpenAPI from comments?
trap: Generated schemas and source comments have different owners; duplicating an authoritative contract creates drift.

assertions.text: Identifies the repository's source of truth for protobuf, OpenAPI, or generated API contracts
Generates derived docs with a pinned, documented tool when appropriate
Keeps hand-written guidance focused on concepts, workflows, and failure modes
Checks generated output in CI or documents when it is intentionally not tracked
